newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt, Jordan hold Hebron talks.
newsitem.headline: Egypt, Jordan hold Hebron talks.

text.p: Jordan's Prime Minister Abdul-Karim al-Kabariti briefed Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak on Monday about a Jordanian-mediated compromise deal on an Israeli withdrawal from most of the occupied West Bank.

Kabariti and Mubarak met as Palestinian and Israeli negotiators tried to wrap up terms for the long-delayed Israeli troop pullback from most of Hebron, the last of seven towns to be handed over to Palestinian self-rule under a 1995 peace deal.
On Sunday, King Hussein flew to Gaza and Tel Aviv on a surprise mediation mission and a Jordanian official said Kabariti would coordinate with Egypt "to keep the ball rolling".

After the meetings with King Hussein, Palestinians and Israelis said the key dispute -- Israel's desire to delay an agreed redeployment in rural areas of the West Bank -- had been resolved with a compromise on the schedule.
Egypt regards itself as an unofficial sponsor of the Middle East peace talks. Palestinian leader Yasser Arafat frequently consults with Mubarak on his negotiations with the Israelis.
Last week, Mubarak met King Hussein in the Egyptian resort town of Aswan to discuss the Hebron negotiations.
